chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, all from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Abu Jameela, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to teach me a supplication for sustenance, so he taught me a supplication which I had not seen more abundant for sustenance than it. He said: Say:

O Allah, grant me from Your extensive Grace a permissible, goodly sustenance, an extensive, permissible, goodly sustenance that suffices for the world and the Hereafter, poured out, welcome, wholesome, without toil and without favor from any of Your creatures, except as an extension from Your extensive Grace, for You said: 'And ask Allah of His Grace'.
So from Your Grace I ask, and from Your Gift I ask, and from Your Full Hand I ask.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia supplication for abundant and permissible sustenance?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication highlights the Shia emphasis on seeking halal provision that ensures spiritual and material sufficiency without the burden of hardship or dependence on creation. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the act of asking directly to the Quranic imperative, reinforcing the theological principle that sustenance is a divine gift accessed through humble petition.
